fp.fragment: anonymous functions and named defs as first-class values
fp.why: Pipelines and callbacks without a class hierarchy.
fp.useWhen: When composition beats a process of loops.
fp.price: Mutation and process state still exist; this is not purity.

sources.quote: Anonymous functions allow us to store and pass executable code around as if it was an integer or a string.
Anonymous functions allow us to store and pass executable code around as if it was an integer or a string.

oop.fragment: no class/prototype OOP in the language core
oop.why: Data is tagged tuples/maps/structs; behaviour is modules and protocols.
oop.useWhen: Do not model a Java-style object graph in Elixir.
oop.price: Protocols are ad-hoc polymorphism, not inheritance.

sources.quote: Protocols are a mechanism to achieve polymorphism in Elixir where you want the behavior to vary depending on the data type.
Protocols are a mechanism to achieve polymorphism in Elixir where you want the behavior to vary depending on the data type.

oop.reason: Elixir is not class-OOP; protocols are not objects/inheritance.

decl.fragment: imperative process loops and functions, not a query/proof language
decl.useWhen: When you need a process to do steps.
decl.price: Pattern matching is not a constraint solver.
decl.reason: Primarily functional/imperative; declaration is not the language model.

actor.fragment: isolated lightweight processes with mailboxes; GenServer is the OTP server pattern
actor.why: Crash isolation and message passing beat shared-memory threads.
actor.useWhen: When you want supervision trees and per-process heaps.
actor.price: Everything copied/shared as messages; no shared Elixir objects.

sources.quote: Processes are isolated from each other, run concurrent to one another and communicate via message passing.
Processes are isolated from each other, run concurrent to one another and communicate via message passing.

static.fragment: dynamically typed; typespecs are documentation/Dialyzer, not compiler-enforced
static.why: Runtime tags over a static checker in the language.
static.useWhen: Scripts and OTP apps; add Dialyzer if the job asks.
static.price: Typespecs are never used by the compiler to optimize or modify code.

sources.quote: Elixir is a dynamically typed language, and as such, type specifications are never used by the compiler to optimize or modify code.
Elixir is a dynamically typed language, and as such, type specifications are never used by the compiler to optimize or modify code.

strong.fragment: strong-dynamic: no JS-style implicit coercions between unlike terms
strong.why: Pattern matching fails instead of silently converting.
strong.price: FFI and binary parsing still have holes.

sources.quote: Elixir is a dynamically typed language, and as such, type specifications are never used by the compiler to optimize or modify code.
Elixir is a dynamically typed language, and as such, type specifications are never used by the compiler to optimize or modify code.

hm.fragment: no Hindley–Milner inference; runtime tags plus optional typespecs
hm.why: The compiler does not infer principal types.
hm.price: Set-theoretic types are experimental and distinct from typespecs.

sources.quote: Elixir is a dynamically typed language, and as such, type specifications are never used by the compiler to optimize or modify code.
Elixir is a dynamically typed language, and as such, type specifications are never used by the compiler to optimize or modify code.

hm.reason: No HM; typespecs are optional and unused by the compiler.

gen.fragment: no parametric generics in the language; protocols are runtime dispatch
gen.why: Polymorphism is protocols/behaviours, not type parameters.
gen.useWhen: When you need per-type behaviour, write a protocol.
gen.price: No reified type parameters at runtime.

sources.quote: Protocols are a mechanism to achieve polymorphism in Elixir where you want the behavior to vary depending on the data type.
Protocols are a mechanism to achieve polymorphism in Elixir where you want the behavior to vary depending on the data type.

gen.reason: No language generics; protocols are not type parameters.

malloc.fragment: authors do not malloc/free Elixir terms
malloc.useWhen: Never as the language memory API.
malloc.price: NIFs can still leak C memory.

sources.quote: Hibernating a GenServer causes garbage collection and leaves a continuous heap that minimises the memory used by the process.
Hibernating a `GenServer` causes garbage collection and leaves a continuous heap that minimises the memory used by the process.

malloc.reason: No malloc/free of Elixir terms; process GC reclaims.

gc.fragment: process-local GC on the VM; GenServer hibernate forces a compacting collection
gc.why: Short-lived process heaps instead of a global stop-the-world app heap.
gc.useWhen: Ordinary Elixir terms; do not free them.
gc.price: A fat process still pauses that process; atoms are never collected.

sources.quote: Hibernating a GenServer causes garbage collection and leaves a continuous heap that minimises the memory used by the process.
Hibernating a `GenServer` causes garbage collection and leaves a continuous heap that minimises the memory used by the process.

trace.fragment: hibernation GC copies live data onto a continuous heap (tracing/copying, not ARC)
trace.useWhen: The default Elixir heap, not Swift ARC.

sources.quote: Hibernating a GenServer causes garbage collection and leaves a continuous heap that minimises the memory used by the process.
Hibernating a `GenServer` causes garbage collection and leaves a continuous heap that minimises the memory used by the process.

rc.fragment: Elixir term heap is not ARC; hibernate/copying GC is the documented Elixir mechanism
rc.why: Do not write retain/release in Elixir.
rc.price: Binary refc lives in the VM, not an Elixir API.

sources.quote: Hibernating a GenServer causes garbage collection and leaves a continuous heap that minimises the memory used by the process.
Hibernating a `GenServer` causes garbage collection and leaves a continuous heap that minimises the memory used by the process.

rc.reason: Not reference-counting as the Elixir heap story.

own.fragment: no borrow checker; isolation is processes, not unique ownership types
own.why: Share by sending, not by aliases.
own.useWhen: Never as a checked unique-ownership language.
own.price: Process dictionary and ETS are explicit sharing.

sources.quote: Processes are isolated from each other, run concurrent to one another and communicate via message passing.
Processes are isolated from each other, run concurrent to one another and communicate via message passing.

thr.fragment: no shared-memory thread+mutex API; lightweight processes, not OS threads
thr.price: Schedulers are VM threads; authors spawn processes.

sources.quote: Elixir's processes should not be confused with operating system processes. Processes in Elixir are extremely lightweight in terms of memory and CPU (even compared to threads
Elixir's processes should not be confused with operating system processes. Processes in Elixir are extremely lightweight in terms of memory and CPU (even compared to threads

thr.reason: No shared-memory thread+mutex model; processes are the unit.

coro.fragment: no async/await colouring; Task.async is another process
coro.why: Concurrency is spawn, not stacked coroutines.
coro.useWhen: When you want overlap, spawn a process/Task.
coro.price: Awaiting a Task still waits on a message.

csp.fragment: mailboxes are actor inboxes, not CSP channels/select as the language
csp.why: Send to a pid, not a first-class channel.
csp.useWhen: Never Go-style chan in the language.
csp.price: Libraries that wrap mailboxes are not CSP.

sources.quote: Processes are isolated from each other, run concurrent to one another and communicate via message passing.
Processes are isolated from each other, run concurrent to one another and communicate via message passing.

loop.fragment: no HTML/Node event loop as the language runtime; GenServer is a process receive loop
loop.price: Blocking a process does not freeze other processes.
loop.reason: No event-loop-as-language-runtime in the Node/HTML sense.
